---
title: "Usage"
---

All the examples on this page show **real results** for the average day of May in
Cuernavaca, Mexico (the EPW and `materials.ini` used here live in `docs/data/` in the
repository). The 1D examples are executed when the site is rendered; the 2D ones are
**pre-computed** — a default-mesh 2D solve takes ~10–20 minutes — by
[`docs/run_examples.py`](https://github.com/Ener-Habitat/EnerHabitat/blob/main/docs/run_examples.py),
whose outputs (in `docs/data/results/`) the page reads and plots. Regenerate them with
`uv run python docs/run_examples.py`.

## Workflow

To simulate a wall (or roof) you need to:

1. **Geolocate it** — pass an EPW file to `Location`.
2. **Orient it** — set `azimuth` (and `tilt` if needed: `90` = wall, `0` = roof).
3. **Define its solar absorptance** — set `absortance` (intuitively the surface
   color, but coatings of the same visible color can differ in absorptance).
4. **Define its layers** — set `layers` from outside to inside.
5. **Choose the period** — call `location.meanDay(month, year)`.
6. **Compute `Tsa()`**, then choose one solver:
   - **`solve()`** — free-running: the indoor temperature `Ti` evolves with the
     dynamics of the constructive system.
   - **`solveAC()`** — air-conditioned: `Ti` is held at the comfort setpoint and the
     cooling/heating energies are reported.

Both solvers return a `pandas.Series` named `"Ti"`, indexed by time of day on the same
time grid as `Tsa()` — so results concatenate directly
(`pd.concat([data, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)` promotes the named Series to a column; no
resampling, no NaN). When a `DataFrame` is required, convert with
`wall.solve().to_frame("Ti")`.

> `Tsa` depends on `absortance`, `tilt`, `azimuth`, the month (`meanDay`) and the
> `Location` — the layer stack does **not** affect it. The setters invalidate the
> cache and the next call to `Tsa()` or to a solver recomputes automatically; a
> prior manual `Tsa()` call is optional (useful to inspect the forcing before
> solving).
>
> One caveat: mutating the stack in place (`wall.layers.append(...)`) bypasses the
> setters, so a later `solve()` can return the cached result of the *previous*
> stack. Assign the full list (`wall.layers = [...]`) or use
> `add_layer()`/`remove_layer()`, which invalidate correctly.

## Recommended folder structure

`materials.ini` is **required** — EnerHabitat ships with no default materials.

```
project/
├── main.py
├── materials.ini      # Material properties (REQUIRED — user-provided)
└── epw/
    ├── ...
    └── example.epw
```

## Materials file

Material properties are declared in an `.ini` file: the material name is the section
header and `k`, `rho`, `c` the keys (case-sensitive, no Greek letters). Inline comments
(`#` or `;`) are allowed. By default the package looks for `materials.ini` in the
working directory; otherwise set `eh.config.file`.

The file below defines **every material used in these docs**, so you can run all the
snippets as-is (values are typical/illustrative — replace with your own data):

```ini
[Adobe]
k   = 0.58    # Thermal conductivity, W/m·K
rho = 1500    # Density, kg/m³
c   = 1480    # Specific heat, J/kg·K

[Mortero]     ; cement mortar / render
k   = 0.70
rho = 1800
c   = 1000

[Ladrillo]    ; fired-clay brick
k   = 0.85
rho = 1600
c   = 840

[Concreto]    ; structural concrete (ribs, topping, hollow block)
k   = 1.80
rho = 2200
c   = 880

[Bovedilla]   ; lightweight filler block
k   = 0.50
rho = 1200
c   = 900

[Yeso]        ; gypsum plaster
k   = 0.37
rho = 900
c   = 1000

[EPS]         ; expanded polystyrene
k   = 0.04
rho = 15
c   = 1400

[Impermeabilizante]   ; asphaltic waterproofing membrane
k   = 0.17
rho = 1100
c   = 1000
```

Assigning a missing path to `config.file` raises `FileNotFoundError` immediately, and
the previously loaded materials (and path) are kept untouched. If the default
`materials.ini` is not present in the working directory when EnerHabitat is imported,
`materials` starts empty (`{}`) — solving then fails because the layer materials
cannot be resolved — so set `config.file` before building systems.

## Examples

The examples form the **system × mode** matrix: 1D/2D, free-running and
air-conditioned. Setup shared by all of them:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
import enerhabitat as eh
import pandas as pd

eh.config.file = "data/materials.ini"
epw_file = "data/MEX_MOR_Cuernavaca-Matamoros.Intl.AP.767260_TMYx.2004-2018.epw"
```

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Plot helper used by the examples (click to show)"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

EH_COLORS = {"Ti": "#2a78d6", "Tsa": "#eb6834", "Ta": "#008300", "Tn": "#6b7280"}
INK = "#374151"

def plot_day(df, cols=("Ta", "Tsa", "Ti"), title=""):
    """Temperatures of the average day, with the comfort zone Tn ± DeltaTn."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 3.6))
    hours = (df.index - df.index[0]).total_seconds() / 3600
    if "Tn" in df and "DeltaTn" in df:
        tn, dtn = float(df["Tn"].iloc[0]), float(df["DeltaTn"].iloc[0])
        ax.axhspan(tn - dtn, tn + dtn, color=EH_COLORS["Tn"], alpha=0.12, lw=0)
        ax.axhline(tn, color=EH_COLORS["Tn"], ls="--", lw=1)
        ax.annotate("comfort  Tn ± ΔTn", xy=(0.4, tn + dtn), va="bottom",
                    fontsize=8, color=INK)
    # end-of-line labels, dodged vertically if two lines end too close
    ends = {c: float(df[c].iloc[-1]) for c in cols}
    span = df[list(cols)].to_numpy()
    min_sep = 0.06 * (span.max() - span.min())
    ypos = dict(ends)
    order = sorted(cols, key=ends.get)
    for a, b in zip(order, order[1:]):
        if ypos[b] - ypos[a] < min_sep:
            ypos[b] = ypos[a] + min_sep
    for c in cols:
        ax.plot(hours, df[c], color=EH_COLORS[c], lw=2, label=c)
        ax.annotate(c, xy=(hours[-1] + 0.4, ypos[c]),
                    va="center", fontsize=9, color=INK)
    ax.set_xlim(0, 26)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 6, 12, 18, 24])
    ax.set_xlabel("hour of the average day")
    ax.set_ylabel("temperature (°C)")
    if title:
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.25, lw=0.5)
    for s in ("top", "right"):
        ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
```

### 1D wall, free-running

```{python}
wall = eh.System(eh.Location(epw_file))
wall.azimuth = 90                    # east-facing
wall.absortance = 0.3
wall.layers = [("Mortero", 0.025), ("Ladrillo", 0.10)]
wall.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
wall.Tsa()

data = wall.solve()                  # free-running Ti
data = pd.concat([data, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)

print(f"energy_transfer = {wall.energy_transfer:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.energy_transfer/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
```

```{python}
plot_day(data, title="Mortero + Ladrillo wall, east, free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

The indoor temperature `Ti` oscillates with a smaller amplitude than the sun–air
temperature `Tsa` and lags behind it — the damping and the delay are the thermal
mass at work.

### 1D wall, air-conditioned

Same wall; `solveAC()` holds `Ti` at the neutrality temperature `Tn` and reports the
energy needed to do so:

```{python}
dataAC = wall.solveAC()
dataAC = pd.concat([dataAC, wall.Tsa()], axis=1)

print(f"cooling_energy = {wall.cooling_energy:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.cooling_energy/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
print(f"heating_energy = {wall.heating_energy:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {wall.heating_energy/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
```

```{python}
plot_day(dataAC, title="Same wall, air-conditioned (Ti = Tn) — May, Cuernavaca")
```

### 2D hollow-block wall, free-running

A concrete block with one air cavity per cell. The 2D element goes **inside** the
layer stack; finishes are ordinary 1D layers around it.

```python
block = eh.HollowBlock(
    material   = "Concreto",          # single material of the block
    emissivity = 0.9,                 # cavity-wall emissivity (radiation)
    geometry   = {                    # cell measures, in metres
        "web":          0.02,         # half web (rib) thickness
        "block_width":  0.16,         # cavity width
        "cover_top":    0.02,         # outer shell
        "cavity":       0.08,         # cavity height
        "cover_bottom": 0.02,         # inner shell
    },
)

wall2d = eh.System2D(eh.Location(epw_file))
wall2d.tilt = 90                      # walls only (required for HollowBlock)
wall2d.azimuth = 90
wall2d.absortance = 0.6
wall2d.layers = [("Mortero", 0.02), block, ("Yeso", 0.01)]
# 2D stacks accept at most 7 layers INCLUDING the 2D element (fixed slots
# inherited from the C engine); exceeding it raises ValueError. 1D has no limit.

wall2d.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
wall2d.Tsa()

ti = wall2d.solve()                   # free-running
# Full results: wall2d.solve_dataframe (Ti, Tso, Tsi, Thueco, °C, on the Tsa grid),
# wall2d.Tfield ((nx, ny) °C field of the last day), wall2d.Qout (J/(m²·day)).
print(wall2d.energy_transfer)         # J/(m²·day), per unit indoor area
```

Pre-computed result of that exact code:

```{python}
import json

RES = "data/results"
summary = json.load(open(f"{RES}/summary.json"))

hollow = pd.read_csv(f"{RES}/hollow_free.csv", index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
s = summary["hollow_free"]
print(f"energy_transfer = {s['energy_transfer']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  ·  converged in {s['days']} days"
      f"  ·  solve time ≈ {s['runtime_s']/60:.0f} min")
plot_day(hollow, title="Hollow-block wall (2D), east, free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

### 2D hollow-block wall, air-conditioned

```python
wall2d.solveAC()                      # Ti held at Tn
print(wall2d.cooling_energy, wall2d.heating_energy)
```

```{python}
hollowAC = pd.read_csv(f"{RES}/hollow_ac.csv", index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
s = summary["hollow_ac"]
print(f"cooling_energy = {s['cooling_energy']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {s['cooling_energy']/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
print(f"heating_energy = {s['heating_energy']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  = {s['heating_energy']/3600:,.0f} Wh/(m²·day)")
plot_day(hollowAC, title="Hollow-block wall (2D), air-conditioned — May, Cuernavaca")
```

### Joist-and-block roof (`Slab`)

Three solids (compression topping, L-shaped rib, filler block) plus N equal cavities
that can be air (`Fill.AIR`) or a solid fill (`Fill.SOLID`).

```python
slab = eh.Slab(
    rib_material     = "Concreto",       # joist/rib (L-shaped: web + foot)
    block_material   = "Bovedilla",      # filler block around the cavities
    topping_material = "Concreto",       # compression topping
    fill_type        = eh.Fill.AIR,      # or eh.Fill.SOLID (+ fill_material)
    emissivity       = 0.9,              # required if AIR
    geometry = {
        "web":          0.025,   # rib web
        "foot":         0.025,   # rib foot
        "shoulder":     0.050,   # block between rib and cavities
        "n_cavities":   3,
        "cavity_width": 0.103,
        "topping":      0.100,   # compression topping
        "topping_cap":  0.050,   # topping above the rib web
        "cover_top":    0.030,   # block above the cavity
        "cavity":       0.040,   # cavity height
        "cover_bottom": 0.030,   # block below the cavity
    },
)

roof = eh.System2D(eh.Location(epw_file))
roof.tilt = 0                            # roofs only (required for Slab)
roof.absortance = 0.3
roof.layers = [("Impermeabilizante", 0.003), slab, ("Yeso", 0.015)]
roof.location.meanDay(month=5, year=2025)
roof.Tsa()

roof.solve()                             # or roof.solveAC()
```

```{python}
slab_df = pd.read_csv(f"{RES}/slab_free.csv", index_col=0, parse_dates=True)
s = summary["slab_free"]
print(f"energy_transfer = {s['energy_transfer']:,.0f} J/(m²·day)"
      f"  ·  converged in {s['days']} days")
plot_day(slab_df, title="Joist-and-block roof (2D), free-running — May, Cuernavaca")
```

Note how the roof's `Tsa` drops **below** `Ta` at night: that is the long-wave
radiation factor ($RF = 3.9$ °C for horizontal surfaces) at work — the roof sees the
cold sky (see [the 1D model](model-1d.qmd#outdoor-boundary-condition-the-sunair-temperature)).

### Filled cavities (`Fill.SOLID`)

The cavity of a `HollowBlock` (or the cavities of a `Slab`) can be filled with a solid
material instead of air — e.g. an insulating core:

```python
block = eh.HollowBlock(
    material      = "Concreto",
    fill_type     = eh.Fill.SOLID,
    fill_material = "EPS",
    geometry      = {"web": 0.02, "block_width": 0.16,
                     "cover_top": 0.02, "cavity": 0.08, "cover_bottom": 0.02},
)
```

Filling with the *same* material as the shell makes the unit homogeneous — equivalent
to a 1D layer (this is one of the package's validation checks).

### Inspecting the section

Before solving you can inspect, **to scale**, how materials and node types are laid
out on the 2D mesh:

```python
wall2d.section_report()            # table: node types + materials (k, ρc, y-range)
wall2d.preview()                   # to-scale panels (node type, k, ρc)
wall2d.preview(field="materials", backend="ascii")   # terminal fallback
sec = wall2d.section()             # NT / k / rhoc arrays + mesh
```

matplotlib is an optional extra (`pip install enerhabitat[viz]`); without it the
inspector falls back to a to-scale ASCII drawing.

## Configuration

### `config` (global)

`config` is a global singleton shared by every `Location` and `System`. Changing it
affects **all** subsequent computations.

| Attribute | Default          | Description |
| --------- | ---------------- | ----------- |
| `file`    | `"materials.ini"`| Path to the `.ini` file with material properties |
| `La`      | `2.5` m          | Depth of the indoor air volume |
| `Nx`      | `200`            | Control volumes across the system thickness |
| `ho`      | `13` W/(m²·K)    | Outdoor film coefficient |
| `hi`      | `8.1` W/(m²·K)   | Indoor film coefficient |
| `dt`      | `10` s *(fixed)* | Time step — **not configurable** (assignments are ignored) |

The `ho`/`hi` defaults are the values prescribed by the Mexican standards
**NOM-008-ENER** and **NOM-020-ENER** (`hi = 8.1` is the vertical-surface value,
applied to all orientations); they can be overridden at any time. `dt` is
locked because of the explicit indoor-air coupling — see
[the numerical method](numerics.qmd#indoor-air-coupling-free-running-mode).

```python
eh.config.file = "./materials.ini"
eh.config.La = 2.0
eh.config.ho = 12          # override the NOM defaults if needed
eh.config.reset()          # restore the numeric defaults (La, Nx, ho, hi, dt, air);
                           # config.file / materials are user-provided and are kept
```

`config.materials` is a read-only dict keyed by material name
(`eh.config.materials["Adobe"].k`, `.rho`, `.c`).

### `config2d` (2D mesh and convergence)

The physics (`La`, `ho`, `hi`, `dt`, air properties) is shared with `config`;
`config2d` holds the 2D-only parameters:

| Attribute   | Default | Description |
| ----------- | ------- | ----------- |
| `nx`        | `80`    | mesh nodes across the cell width (adiabatic sides) |
| `ny`        | `160`   | mesh nodes through the thickness (outside → inside) |
| `tol_inner` | `1e-8` °C | inner-step tolerance (max node update **and** max equation residual) |
| `tol_day`   | `5e-4` °C | day-to-day convergence tolerance |
| `max_days`  | `60`    | cap on the day-to-day iterations |
| `max_inner` | `10000` | cap on inner sweeps per step (hit → `converged = False`) |

```python
from enerhabitat import config2d
config2d.nx, config2d.ny = 120, 160
```

> Each solve is single-threaded. For volume (many configurations), parallelise at the
> **process level** — run independent `solve()` calls in separate processes
> (`multiprocessing`, `joblib`); this scales near-linearly (≈6× at 8 processes). See
> [Performance](numerics.qmd#performance).
